thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: kv-cache eviction rate x6, host paging and degraded p99s for /generate on us-west-2-GPUpool 
ops-bot: affected: 12 hosts, 3 OOM kill events, continuous-batcher queue depth spike. runbook: https://console.internal/incidents/1932506789 

Ava R.: oncall, ack. I'm grabbing the triage. please add customer impact if you see it. 

Jamal K.: quick summary from initial probe — rolled quantization kernel changes yesterday (awq int8 path) and a kernel-selection tweak that changes KV packing. combined with continuous-batching change that bumps avg seq_len, KV per-request doubled in many cases. overall mem blowup -> swap/paging -> eviction storms. 

Priya S.: timeline matches: deploy at 03:10 UTC yesterday (awq-int8-kernel), batching tweak at 05:40 (increase batch_max_tokens to 4096). saw steady rise overnight. 

Miguel L.: customer-facing note: CS reported elevated 504/timeout for a handful of Dedicated customers on us-west. not yet a large outage but definitely increased latency and errors. informing them now. 

Ava R.: immediate mitigation suggestions? 

Priya S.: suggested hotfixs (in order):
1) disable AWQ int8 kernel selection for affected model variant (fallback to gptq/int16).
2) reduce continuous-batcher config: batch_max_tokens -> 1024, batch_max_requests -> 8
3) bump kv-eviction aggressiveness (decrease ttl, lower soft_limit) for the pool until stable
4) monitor for errors, then can progressively re-enable if safe

Jamal K.: I can flip kernel feature-flag now. command: 
```
# toggle feature flag for awq path on model my-model:v2026-03-14
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" 
  https://api.internal/admin/models/my-model/flags 
  -d '{"awq_enabled":false}'
```

Miguel L.: I'll send the reduced batching config to infra autoscaler: 
```
PATCH /api/internal/pools/us-west-2-GPUpool/config
{ "continuous_batching": { "batch_max_tokens": 1024, "batch_max_requests": 8 } }
```

Ava R.: Priya, Jamal — please proceed. I'm coordinating customer comms. SRE Lead, can you watch the nodes for paging? 

SRE Lead: watching. enabling emergency eviction policy now. 

ops-bot: ACTION: rolled awq flag -> false on 9/12 hosts at 1932506890. applied batch config to pool at 1932506945. eviction policy tightened at 1932507001. 

Jamal K.: quick verify: p99 for /generate dropped from 1.8s -> 310ms on sampled hosts within 90s of the change. eviction rate normalized. memory headroom restored. 

Priya S.: logs: saw immediate drop in KV allocation per request. paging counters -> zero. GPU memory utilization back to baseline. no further OOMs. 

Miguel L.: customer update: notified 4 Dedicated customers, offering followup and timeline. engineering contacted product to coordinate any credits if needed. 

Ava R.: handing off to next oncall for monitoring and follow-ups. items for follow-up and owners: 
- postmortem + root cause: Jamal K. + Priya S.
- regression test for quant kernel packing & KV size: eng-runtime (Miguel L.)
- safety gate for batching config + canary profile: SRE Lead
- customer impact summary & comms: Miguel L. + CS

SRE Lead: assigned, will open incident doc and postmortem checklist. 

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) at 1932507120 — service performance stable, keep monitoring for 2 hours. 

Ava R.: thanks team. action items: do not re-enable awq-int8 kernel until we validate KV packing/size across seq distributions and kernel selection fallback. create test harness to simulate long-concat workloads.

Jamal K.: noted. will add instrumentation to measure per-request KV bytes. planning a canary re-run with staged kernel selector and tight telemetry. ETA for follow-up: 48h. 

Priya S.: adding runbook blurb: when kernel changes are merged, require kv-size regression < 10% on long-seq synthetic workloads.

Miguel L.: closing loop with customers, will add timeline to CS ticket. 

Ava R.: handoff complete. next oncall: @SRE Lead. react with :white_check_mark: when you have accepted. 

SRE Lead: :white_check_mark: accepted. closing thread once postmortem doc is created. 

(threads, reactions: multiple :eyes:, :thumbsup:)
